# Avatar · image · mask · idol

## #0

Presence becomes addressable through a form. A face turns towards someone; a name lets that person be called again; a gesture carries an intention into a shared situation. A role gives an undertaking a recognisable place. Someone can now be met, remembered, trusted, opposed or answered. The form's finitude lets this encounter occur here, between these participants. Its success can also turn into possession when the presentation acquires authority over the life it makes available.

Finite form gives the encounter its mediation. A person does not first become complete in isolation and subsequently add a public mask. Language, bodily expression, histories of recognition and shared practices participate in the life that appears. Yet no achieved presentation finishes that life. The person who was named can answer differently; the person remembered can have changed; the one approached through a role can question what the role permits. Maintained personhood is this consequential continuity through different appearances, including the capacity to alter how one is received.

Taylor's avatar–image–mask–idol programme develops one authored ecology through four distinguishable offices. Avatar concerns presence becoming effective in a finite appearance. Image concerns the particular formation that gathers attention and value. Mask concerns the presentation through which participation becomes possible. Idol concerns the closure by which a successful formation takes possession of the authority it was meant to mediate. These offices can meet in one form; their relation is not a historical claim that four traditions tell one story.

The complete relation articulated in [Taylor's core](../../../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md) unfolds as parent `/ = −/−`, `0/1`, `?/!`, `−/+`, `X/x`, `AM/IS`, `∞/dx`, and return `1/0`. A form arises within that movement and carries its source into a particular appearance. Question can address assertion; an instance can expose the capacity through which it was formed; the personed encounter can change the account; the achieved account can return as a condition of another determination. Avatar, image, mask and idol distinguish what happens to presence, force, participation and authority within this relation. Their four offices do not add positions to the native eight.

## #1

The avatar brings a wider presence into a particular encounter. In this authored use, descent names the movement into a form that can act: a voice rather than every possible voice, a gesture rather than intention without expression, an entrusted representative rather than an undertaking with no bearer. The presence is not made unreal by having an appearance. It acquires an occasion on which it can matter.

That occasion preserves a difference of office. A representative can speak authoritatively within a commission; the representative's statement remains answerable to what was entrusted. Even the original instruction is already a formulation. It cannot exhaust the intention simply because it was written first. Within [authored delegation](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A28-Authored-Ground-Positional-Delegation.md), a human, institution or agent occupies a source-position relative to a commission. That bearer remains situated within a wider field, and the prompt through which they commission another act is already a determination. An encounter can therefore return upon the formulated instruction or its governing purpose without making the earliest wording an absolute source. Authority can be exact and effective without becoming absolute sourcehood.

The avatar's body belongs to the encounter it enters. A voice needs someone who can hear it; a gesture acquires consequences in a shared situation; an entrusted representative inherits a commission and answers through what the representation does. The source relation passes into action, where another participant can accept, question or refuse it. That response becomes part of the form's history. Taylor's avatar names this effective finite presence. The histories of Sanskrit avatāra and theological descent would require their own doctrines and passages before this authored relation could be attributed to them.

An image makes that presence available under a particular arrangement. The arrangement can be faithful without being exhaustive. A remembered face, an emblem or a written account selects; selection gives recognition its precision. The source/reflection distinction also has direction. A reflection can be encountered first in time while remaining dependent on what it reflects. Within a declared Context Frame, an achieved image or source record can genuinely occupy **Bimba**, the local original against which further readings are compared. The same field occupies **pratibimba**, situated reflection, relative to its wider sources. In this [Bimba–Pratibimba relation](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C38-Bimba-Pratibimba-Bimba-Map.md), the local original gives agreement and error a definite reference, and what those comparisons return can revise that original itself. Its authority is real at the scale of the inquiry. Idolisation begins when it prevents its own source relation from being questioned or changed.

The interpreting agent occupies the functional knower office in a local comparison. Its reference image, remembered encounters, rules and instruments are the means; the represented person, source claims and alternative readings are known. The agent's selection can itself become known in a further inquiry. In the containing person's Life, this complete apparatus serves as means through which an appearance can be met and judged. The relative offices let the image act without confusing its useful authority with the whole relation in which the person encounters it.

## #2

The image gathers force. Attention returns to it; desire and fear organise themselves around it; expectations begin to make some possibilities vivid and others difficult to receive. A picture that once expressed a situation can become a measure for the next situation. The person making or interpreting it is changed through that activity. The formation acquires a history, and its later efficacy includes what its earlier appearances have done.

In [Taylor’s reading of symbolic transformation](../../../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-symbolon-dynamics/taylor-2026-symbolon-dynamics.md), archetypal capacity, particular image and organising complex keep different offices within this reciprocal movement. An archetype is not one finished portrait; an image is not the whole capacity from which further images can arise; a complex organises a field of response around a consequential formation. Attention, libido, desire and valuation name different aspects or registers of that efficacy. Their relation here does not turn them into interchangeable physical energies.

In the [Neumann articulation](../../../archetypal-ground/neumann-images/WHOLE.md), the round holds the parental relation before its differentiated figures appear. Nourishing and engulfing faces of origin give dependence its contrary possibilities; separation of the world parents opens a world in which powers can be distinguished. The hero gains an effective position within that world, then encounters the limits of identifying life with the victorious image. Transformation returns the achieved differentiation into relation with what it had subordinated or excluded. Each formation carries a capacity that its own established image can subsequently confine.

Taylor's encounter with [Neumann](../../../../episteme/sources/psychology/neumann/neumann-1954-origins-history-consciousness/neumann-1954-origins-history-consciousness.md) extends the relation through the whole native field: relation, conscious circumstance, question and assertion, withdrawal and extension, determining capacity and instance, personed context, differential horizon and return. The complementary folds remain active within this movement: question answers in a personed world, felt force acquires a readable pattern, and the conscious circumstance retains its inexhaustible depth. The condition of appearing precedes an ego's achieved self-image. Neumann's ego-development sequence has a distinct psychological office; it neither limits this native relation to ego chronology nor assigns each culture a position on that sequence.

The image's efficacy reaches the body as well as its account. In Taylor's *Symbolon Dynamics*, libido concerns psychic investment and valuation; prāṇa concerns living circulation through breath, rhythm and differentiated current; Śakti concerns manifestation-power, including the concealment of source within its formation and its return through recognition. A repeated image can gather desire, alter the rhythm of attention and make a once-unavailable response possible. These registers disclose different operations of that efficacy. Their coordination belongs to Taylor's synthesis; their names do not license a common physical measurement or transfer one tradition's evidence into another.

An image's success therefore creates the pressure that will test it. A form that has held a life together has a claim upon attention. Revising it can threaten a valued coherence, an institution's continuity or a familiar account of oneself. The test concerns what this coherence can receive. If a new encounter changes the meaning, valuation or jurisdiction of the image, symbolic efficacy remains alive. If every encounter must confirm it, the interpreter's apparent fidelity begins to protect the image from the relation that made it significant.

[Image, Valuation and Possession](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A20-Image-Valuation-Possession.md) become distinguishable through this change in authority. An image mediates while its source relation remains active; idolisation appropriates that relation. A vivid or beloved image is not thereby an idol. Nor does a quiet, abstract or apparently rational account escape the test. The decisive change is in authority: whether the encountered source can still alter what the image is allowed to mean and do.

## #3

The image becomes a mask when it offers a way to enter a social field. Language, manner, clothing, credentials and the expectations of a role make someone legible to others. A mask can protect an intimacy, sustain a public obligation or let a person exercise capacities that would otherwise have no recognised place. Learning to wear it is an achievement of participation. There is no demand here for a person to become completely exposed in order to be real.

The pressure appears when access depends upon the presentation so completely that its bearer must administer life according to the recognising field's measure. What began as an interface becomes an internal criterion. The person anticipates what will count, edits what can be shown and may come to receive an unapproved response as a defect in the self. The mask continues to open doors while narrowing the life that can pass through them. This is a possible passage within self-administration; a clinical diagnosis or a claim about every social role would require evidence of the particular person and situation.

The mask/chameleon seam retains a specific pressure: adaptation can grant access while requiring a bearer to reproduce the measure that renders parts of that bearer illegible. The surrounding field acts through the person's acquired skill in navigating it. Participation can become self-administration through that success. Racial and colonial histories involve specific coercion, language, bodies and institutions; a Fanonian or biographical comparison must preserve those conditions rather than replace them with this general relation.

The distinction is sharply staged in [*The Prisoner*](../../../../episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/mcgoohan-markstein/mcgoohan-markstein-1967-the-prisoner/mcgoohan-markstein-1967-the-prisoner.md). After resignation, an unnamed intelligence agent is abducted into the Village and designated Number Six. Changing occupants hold the office of Number Two; the identity of Number One remains the question. When Six asks who One is, the answer assigns Six his place. Numbering gives the administrative office continuity across its occupants and gives the captive an identity the institution can administer. The question about power's source has been diverted into power's classification of the questioner.

The series' concluding *Fall Out* returns this question through masks and Six's own face, then through escape and an unresolved London return. That inward turn does not cancel the Village's coercive apparatus or declare captivity imaginary. The finale sequence here follows written witnesses; its exact audiovisual continuity requires timecode collation. In Taylor's refraction the return reaches both the institution and the claimant to sovereignty within the person. Replacing an administrator or removing a mask does not alone make the governing relation answerable. Number Two and Number Six retain their dramatic offices; they supply no proof of the native `4+2` generation.

## #4

The idol closes the path through the image. The bearer remains visible, perhaps more widely represented than before, while losing the ability to change the terms under which the representation acts. The category is permitted to know the person before encounter. Contrary speech is then classified as further evidence of the category. The image need not become inaccurate in every detail. Its protected jurisdiction lets even an accurate local description govern what exceeds that description.

Ovid's [Apollo and Daphne sequence](../../../../episteme/sources/classical-philology/ovid/ovid-1921-metamorphoses-miller/ovid-1921-metamorphoses-miller.md) gives this continued efficacy an exact body. Apollo's boast after Python leads to Cupid's opposed arrows. Daphne's prior refusal of marriage and Peneus's grant of that wish precede the pursuit. Apollo's powers do not make his desire hers. Exhaustion, appeal and transformation end with the laurel: the changed body is still felt as living, recoils from the kiss, and is claimed for Apollo's emblems. The ending also gives the tree an appearance of assent. The recoil and apparent assent give the ending its tension; their conjunction does not turn the pursuit into uncomplicated consent. The authored image–idol reading concerns the emblem's power to continue after possession of the living other has failed. Roman literary telling, its Greek figures and its later interpretation retain different places and times.

The [biblical Job witness](../../../../episteme/sources/biblical-studies/anonymous/biblical-job-kjv-ebible-eng-kjv2006/biblical-job-kjv-ebible-eng-kjv2006.md) tests a different image: an account of divine justice. The councils, successive losses, bodily affliction and wife's challenge precede the friends' explanations. Eliphaz, Bildad and Zophar first mourn and sit silently with Job; their later advocacy must be read against that initial accompaniment. Job's protest and defence of integrity resist an explanation which would require him to become the guilty person it needs. Wisdom in chapter 28 exceeds extraction and purchase; Elihu's separate intervention precedes the whirlwind. The divine speeches bring a world and creatures beyond Job's administration without explaining the councils to him. His response is followed by the friends' rebuke and their need for his intercession. Renewed household and social life do not erase the first children's deaths.

The defence of the account changes when Job can be heard and its advocates must receive his mediation. Jung's [*Answer to Job* comparison, §§614–617](../../../../episteme/sources/psychology/jung/jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11/jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11.md#jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q002) has a separate office: he reads the treatment of the faithful witness as a crisis of the God-image requiring self-reflection and remembrance of Sophia. That is an attributed psychological interpretation. Sophia is not introduced as an actor in biblical Job 28, and Jung's reconstruction does not become Taylor's native derivation. The three registers meet through a stated relation without losing their tellings.

<a id="avatar-counterfeit-provenance"></a>
The subordinate **deepfake as counterfeit Symbolon** carries the closure into the claimed seam itself. In the exact quilt passage, the apparent relation joins body to utterance, event to recording, speaker to voice, source to sign. A fabricated recording presented as a witness claims that this person spoke or this event occurred in the represented way. The counterfeit is more than a false proposition: it forges the apparent provenance by which the proposition asks to be trusted. A disclosed fictional construction has a different source claim and must be judged under that claim.

The next turn reaches the genuine record. Once fabrication is available as an explanation, a real witness can be dismissed as another synthetic appearance. The apparent source relation is attacked first by counterfeiting it and then by making the possibility of counterfeiting a reason to refuse its genuine instance. This is the locally argued second-order mechanism, often named the liar's dividend in the developmental passage; no prevalence, magnitude or documented media case is established here. Those empirical claims require independent evidence.

The [Primordial Symbolon](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A18-Primordial-Symbolon-and-Its-Eight-Determinations.md) joins source and sign; a counterfeit fabricates that apparent slash rather than merely asserting something false. The image then appropriates source authority through the claim that it records a person or event. Its circulation changes what will be admitted in the next encounter. [The Mirror That Moves First](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A32-Reflective-Field-The-Mirror-That-Moves-First.md) initiates the contrary turn: the instrument exposes the source, angle and measure of its answer before requiring the addressed person to conform. The counterfeited relation and the genuinely disclosed relation therefore have different consequences for what can next be trusted.

## #5→0

Regard returns through the form to the participant who can answer it. The answer need not confirm the first question. It can disclose an omitted circumstance, refuse an imposed role, correct an attributed statement or show that the criterion itself has misnamed the encounter. The result is another determination with a changed history. Maintained personhood does not require an essence displayed without mediation; it requires that continuity of address not become ownership of the person addressed.

The [Arbitration / Hybris / Regard / Anamnesis relation](../../../../episteme/etymologies/arbitration-hybris-regard-anamnesis/WHOLE-FIELD-arbitration-hybris-regard-anamnesis.md) gives this return six connected operations. Continuity-in-Indeterminacy retains what a presentation cannot finish; Criterion-through-Distinction makes its measure available; Delineation-through-Difference locates its frame. Arbitration-in-Crisis brings a consequential decision. Con-text-through-Diaphaneity lets the other and the framing conditions become visible through that decision. Resolution-in-Reconciliation returns the settlement with its history. Regard receives the person affected by the judgment; anamnesis lets the achieved history participate in another act. Their conjunction is an operational relation, with each word's lexical ancestry remaining distinct.

The [Symbol / Account / Trust relation](../../../../episteme/etymologies/symbol-account-and-trust/WHOLE-FIELD-symbol-account-and-trust.md) carries four further operations. A symbol answers to the source it claims to bear. An account makes that claim inspectable while the person's standing continues beyond the report. Trust keeps correction, refusal and consequences capable of reaching the governing office. What the image has done re-enters its source-field as a condition of its next use. Provenance, signatures, audits and credentials can strengthen specified evidential relations. Persons and institutions undertake responsibility for how those relations are used and for the answer they receive.

An entrusted avatar can therefore remain powerful through situated delegation. Its source office is inspectable and revisable. A mask can continue to enable participation while allowing its bearer to exceed and alter its terms. An image can remain beloved while acquiring another meaning, or survive as an acknowledged historical sign after its former symbolic life has ended. A received answer can warrant correction, renewed reliance on a fitting condition, or withdrawal. Neither fidelity nor return obliges the bearer to continue an injurious encounter. Withdrawal can itself be the answer the representation must learn to receive.

The person, the image and the shared field return still distinct, with the warranted judgment carried into the next encounter. [Self and Other](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A27-Self-and-Other-Unity-without-Possession.md) belong within one whole while no participant owns the other's reply. Through [Objective Co-Internality](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A30-Objective-Co-Internality.md), one encounter enters several participants' later conditions. Neumann's differentiated participation gives this change a psychological comparison without making ego chronology the limit of the native operation. The image has carried a presence into life. Its continuing integrity lies in allowing that life to answer back.

### Source relations and limits

Taylor's four-office ecology places finite presence, valued image, participating mask and appropriated authority in one relation. Daphne, Job and Number Six give that relation different bodies; counterfeit provenance locates a further closure in the apparent source-link itself. These comparisons preserve their distinct tellings rather than identify ancient divine descent with a software persona.

In [Apollo–Eros–Daphne–Peneus](../../roman-latin/apollo-eros-daphne-peneus/WHOLE.md), the emblem retains power after the pursued body has withdrawn; [Job](../../biblical/job/WHOLE.md) becomes the witness and intercessor whom the defended account must finally hear; [The Prisoner](../../british-television/the-prisoner/WHOLE.md) joins numbering, institutional continuity and an unresolved return through the sovereign mask. Their fuller movements and aftermaths let mediation's capacity to capture what it makes present be compared without reducing the figures to interchangeable examples.

Geography and time follow different relations here. Taylor's 2026 authorial world gathers the comparisons. Ovid's Roman literary work carries Greek figures; Job's narrated land of Uz, the biblical book and its later English witness have separate identities; the Village and London are dramatic places in a 1967–68 British television work. Neumann's twentieth-century psychological reception supplies shared structuration rather than a geographical origin for these works. Their conjunction follows the image's operation without proposing historical transmission among the examples.

[Parātrīśikā-Vivaraṇa](../../../../episteme/sources/indian-philosophy/abhinavagupta/abhinavagupta-singh-1988-paratrisika-vivarana/abhinavagupta-singh-1988-paratrisika-vivarana.md) relates Word, communication and subjectivity through Singh's introduction and translation, distinguished from Abhinavagupta's commentary. The retained notebook passages support those relations; attributing this avatar ecology to an exact avatāra doctrine or icon–idol history would require the corresponding primary passages. [Aion](../../../../episteme/sources/psychology/jung/jung-1978-aion-cw9-2/jung-1978-aion-cw9-2.md) concerns Self and symbolic totality in the selected passages; they do not establish a particular historical theory of persona. Taylor's protected Neumann encounter and selected-copy quotations keep their authorial and quotation standing distinct. The CW11 passage above supports Jung's God-image interpretation as paraphrase.
